title: Cardano gets custom USD stablecoins, but minus the customers — What should you know?
summary: Brale's launch connects Cardano to 30 blockchains, but no issuers have been named yet.
content: Brale has launched custom USD stablecoins on the Cardano network, connecting the blockchain to thirty other networks. However, the launch currently lacks specific issuers or customers. This development expands Cardano's cross-chain capabilities, though its practical adoption and usage will depend on future stablecoin issuers joining the platform.
content_ta: Brale நிறுவனம் Cardano நெட்வொர்க்கில் தனிப்பயன் USD stablecoins-ஐ அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இதன் மூலம் இந்த பிளாக்செயின் முப்பது பிற நெட்வொர்க்குகளுடன் இணைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. இருப்பினும், இந்த தொடக்கக் கட்டத்தில் குறிப்பிட்ட issuers அல்லது வாடிக்கையாளர்கள் யாரும் இன்னும் பெயரிடப்படவில்லை. இந்த வளர்ச்சி Cardano-வின் குறுக்கு-சங்கிலி திறன்களை விரிவுபடுத்துகிறது.

title: LayerZero adds Samsung Card, Kakao Pay, ZAN as validators for upcoming Zero blockchain
summary: Zero uses ZK proofs to separate execution from verification, removing a layer of redundancy by leaving validators to only verify the proofs.
content: LayerZero has integrated major financial and tech brands, including Samsung Card, Kakao Pay, and ZAN, as validators for its upcoming Zero blockchain. The Zero network utilizes zero-knowledge proofs to separate transaction execution from verification. This approach eliminates redundancy by allowing validators to focus exclusively on verifying the cryptographic proofs.
content_ta: வரவிருக்கும் தனது Zero blockchain-க்கான வேலிடேட்டர்களாக Samsung Card, Kakao Pay மற்றும் ZAN போன்ற முக்கிய நிறுவனங்களை LayerZero சேர்த்துள்ளது. Zero நெட்வொர்க் ஆனது பரிவர்த்தனை நிறைவேற்றுதலை சரிபார்ப்பிலிருந்து பிரிக்க ZK proofs-ஐப் பயன்படுத்துகிறது. வேலிடேட்டர்கள் சரிபார்ப்பு பணிகளில் மட்டும் கவனம் செலுத்த அனுமதிக்கிறது.

title: Bitcoin Lightning operators could recover stuck payments even after losing channel data

The 26.12 release candidate can help recover eligible funds after channel data loss if the operator still has key records and can get help from the peer.

Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox

This development addresses a significant vulnerability for Lightning Network users, offering a path to recover assets that were previously considered permanently inaccessible after local data corruption.
content_ta: Bitcoin Lightning nodes-ன் புதிய பதிப்பான 26.12, சேனல் டேட்டா இழப்பு ஏற்பட்டாலும் சிக்கியுள்ள பணத்தை மீட்டெடுக்கும் வசதியை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. நோட் ஆபரேட்டர்கள் தங்களின் முக்கிய ரெக்கார்டுகளை வைத்திருந்து, மற்றொறு பயனரின் உதவியைப் பெறுவதன் மூலம் நிதியை மீட்டெடுக்க முடியும். இந்த மேம்பாடு, மின்னல் நெட்வொர்க் (Lightning Network) பயனர்களுக்கு ஒரு முக்கிய தீர்வாக அமையும், ஏனெனில் முன்னதாக இத்தகைய டேட்டா இழப்பினால் நிதி நிரந்தரமாக முடக்கப்படும் சூழல் இருந்தது.

title: Bitcoin ETFs shed $4 billion — How did one fund hide the cracks before leading the exit?
summary: If one fund carries 84% of the exits, what exactly is the industry headline measuring?
content: Bitcoin ETFs have reported $4 billion in outflows, but market data reveals a skewed picture. One single fund is responsible for 84% of these withdrawals, raising questions about whether aggregate headlines accurately reflect the broader industry sentiment. While the massive exit from this specific fund dominates the narrative, the rest of the sector shows a significantly different trend, suggesting the headline figure may not represent the overall health of Bitcoin investment products.
content_ta: Bitcoin ETF-களில் இருந்து $4 பில்லியன் வெளியேறியுள்ளதாக தகவல்கள் தெரிவிக்கின்றன. ஆனால், இதில் 84 சதவீத வெளியேற்றம் ஒரே ஒரு ஃபண்டினால் மட்டுமே நடந்துள்ளது. ஒட்டுமொத்த சந்தையின் போக்கை இந்த ஒரு ஃபண்டின் தரவுகள் தவறாக சித்தரிக்கிறதா என்ற கேள்வி எழுந்துள்ளது. ஒட்டுமொத்த முதலீட்டுச் சந்தையின் உண்மையான நிலையை, இந்த தலைப்புச் செய்திகள் பிரதிபலிக்கிறதா அல்லது ஒரு குறிப்பிட்ட ஃபண்டின் செயல்பாட்டை மட்டும் பெரிதுபடுத்துகிறதா என்பது தற்போது விவாதமாகியுள்ளது.

content_ta: Bank of Korea தனது வட்டி விகிதத்தை 3.25% ஆக உயர்த்தியுள்ளது. title: CertiK Finds 38 Hidden AI Bugs That Could Cost the Industry Millions
summary:
Researchers at CertiK and Columbia University have discovered 38 bugs in software that performs some of the most fundamental calculations behind modern AI.  Among them are two bugs in DeepSeek’s DeepGEMM library and 23 in FlashAttention, a widely used technology that makes AI models run faster. One of these bugs went undetected through 17,760 runs
The post CertiK Finds 38 Hidden AI Bugs That Could Cost the Industry Millions appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: Researchers from CertiK and Columbia University have identified 38 critical software bugs embedded within the foundations of modern AI technology. The flaws, found in widely used libraries such as DeepSeek’s DeepGEMM and FlashAttention, could lead to significant financial risks for the industry. Some of these vulnerabilities remained undetected despite thousands of rigorous testing cycles, highlighting a pressing need for enhanced security measures in the rapidly evolving artificial intelligence landscape.
content_ta: CertiK மற்றும் Columbia University ஆராய்ச்சியாளர்கள் இணைந்து நவீன AI தொழில்நுட்பத்தின் அடிப்படையான மென்பொருட்களில் 38 முக்கிய பிழைகளைக் கண்டறிந்துள்ளனர். DeepSeek நிறுவனத்தின் DeepGEMM மற்றும் FlashAttention போன்ற பரவலாகப் பயன்படுத்தப்படும் தொழில்நுட்பங்களில் இந்த பிழைகள் கண்டறியப்பட்டுள்ளன. இதனால் தொழில்துறைக்கு பெரும் நிதி இழப்பு ஏற்படும் அபாயம் உள்ளது. ஆயிரக்கணக்கான சோதனைகளுக்குப் பிறகும் சில பிழைகள் கண்டறியப்படாமல் இருந்திருப்பது, AI தொழில்நுட்பத்தின் பாதுகாப்பில் அதிக கவனம் செலுத்த வேண்டியதன் அவசியத்தை வலியுறுத்துகிறது.

title: Anthropic and OpenAI proofs fuel speculation about AI’s threat to encryption
summary:
AI advancements in solving complex mathematical problems could undermine current encryption systems, posing significant security risks.
The post Anthropic and OpenAI proofs fuel speculation about AI’s threat to encryption appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Recent mathematical proofs demonstrated by Anthropic and OpenAI have sparked significant concern regarding the future of data security. title: Fidelity Files for Chainlink ETF. What Does It Mean for LINK?
summary: Key takeaways Fidelity has filed to launch a Chainlink ETF (ticker FLNK) that would hold LINK directly and list on Nasdaq, but the filing is preliminary with no launch date or final fee. The fund would not stake its LINK, so shareholders would not receive staking rewards. Fidelity would enter a market that already has Grayscale (GLNK) and Bitwise (CLNK) LINK funds, and Charles Schwab offers direct LINK trading. A new listing does not automatically mean new LINK buying: only sustained net creations add to the fund’s holdings. Shares outstanding, LINK held and net creations after launch will show whether demand is genuinely new. Fidelity’s Chainlink ETF proposal would hold LINK directly and trade on Nasdaq if it clears the remaining steps. The proposed Fidelity Chainlink Fund, described in a November 25 registration statement, would use the ticker FLNK, although the filing is preliminary and no launch date or final annual fee has been provided. The larger question is not whether Wall Street can package LINK. It already has. The question is whether Fidelity can attract fresh demand for the token rather than divide the existing market among another set of fund shares. Fidelity’s Filing Is Specific About What Investors Would Own The proposed fund would hold LINK, not a basket of blockchain companies or derivatives intended to mimic LINK’s price. Its objective is to follow the token’s U.S. dollar performance, less expenses and liabilities. The prospectus identifies Anchorage Digital Bank, BitGo Bank & Trust and Coinbase Custody as custodians, with the trust intending to hold its LINK on Ethereum. Fidelity also lays out how the price would be measured. Its proposed reference rate uses prices from eligible LINK spot markets, with a volume-weighted median methodology calculated every 15 seconds using rolling 60-minute market data. That is a mechanism for valuing the assets. It is not a guarantee that fund shares will trade at precisely the reported value when markets are thin or volatile. Nor is this a yield product. The filing states plainly: “The Trust will not stake its LINK.” Shareholders would not receive staking rewards through the fund. They would be buying securities designed to reflect an underlying token’s price, not a wallet balance they can use in Chainlink services. That distinction matters because the company’s use of Chainlink technology elsewhere is a separate story. NewsBTC has previously reported on Chainlink infrastructure used with Fidelity’s tokenized FILQ fund. An investment vehicle that owns LINK is not evidence of increased demand for Chainlink’s oracle services, and using the network’s technology does not automatically mean buying its token. Fidelity Would Enter a Market That Already Has LINK Funds This is not the first attempt to make LINK available through conventional securities accounts. Grayscale’s Chainlink Trust ETF, trading as GLNK, had a share creation and redemption program in place from December 2025, according to its SEC disclosures. The Bitwise Chainlink ETF, CLNK, also appeared in a January 2026 Nasdaq information circular. And fund shares are not the only conventional route. In November, NewsBTC covered Charles Schwab’s rollout of direct LINK trading to eligible crypto clients. These routes do different things, but they establish a useful baseline: access is no longer the same problem it was when crypto products were confined to specialist exchanges. Fidelity’s possible advantage is distribution. Its name and brokerage relationships may reach customers who would not open a crypto wallet or buy LINK on a trading platform. That is a credible reason the filing matters. But branding, however recognizable, cannot tell investors how much money will arrive once trading begins. There is also the price of access. The preliminary prospectus leaves the sponsor’s annual fee blank. Until that figure is settled, it is impossible to make an honest cost comparison with competing LINK products. For investors choosing between wrappers around the same token, fees, trading spreads and the gap between share prices and net asset value deserve more attention than a new ticker. A New ETF Listing Would Not Automatically Mean New LINK Buying The mechanics are worth getting right. The proposed trust would issue and redeem large blocks of shares through authorized participants, using cash or LINK under procedures described in the filing. Everyday investors would generally trade the shares on an exchange instead of placing orders with the trust. Those are two different markets. When one investor sells an existing fund share to another, the trade does not by itself require the trust to acquire more LINK. Sustained net creations can increase a fund’s underlying holdings. Redemptions can do the reverse. A rising share price, meanwhile, may reflect a higher LINK price rather than additional tokens entering custody. That is why the announcement alone provides no evidence of fresh institutional inflows. The Form S-1 is a plan, not a subscription report. It does not tell us how much outside capital will be committed, what portion might come from rival products, or whether investor interest will survive a difficult crypto market. There is a fair counterargument. Fidelity could appeal to a materially different pool of investors and grow total demand rather than simply redistribute it. The filing establishes a possible channel for that to happen. It does not establish the outcome. What Would Actually Change the Assessment? First, the registration statement must become effective and the proposed Nasdaq listing must move forward. The final prospectus should also resolve the missing fee and other commercial details. Those are immediate milestones, not formalities to be assumed away. If the product launches, the more revealing evidence will arrive afterward: the number of LINK held, changes in shares outstanding, sustained net creations or redemptions, trading liquidity and discounts or premiums to net asset value. Comparisons with existing LINK funds would help separate fresh demand from investors moving between products. Until those figures exist, the sensible interpretation is narrow. Fidelity wants to sell investors exposure to Chainlink through a familiar brokerage format. Whether that changes the market for LINK is still an open question, and one that a filing cannot answer.
content: Fidelity Investments has filed for a new Chainlink ETF, dubbed FLNK, aiming to provide direct exposure to the token on Nasdaq. While the proposal highlights Fidelity’s distribution reach, it remains preliminary without a finalized fee or launch date. The fund will not offer staking rewards. Whether this product attracts significant new institutional demand or simply fragments existing market liquidity among current providers like Grayscale and Bitwise remains to be seen after its potential launch.

title: Bitcoin’s Recovery Faces a New Warning After $2 Billion in ETF Outflows
summary: Key takeaways US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $2.05 billion in combined net outflows over four straight sessions ending November 24, per Farside Investors, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for roughly $1.77 billion. Bitcoin is back above $60,000 after trading as low as about $55,300 on November 21, according to Glassnode. Reclaiming $60,000 does not by itself confirm the correction is over: holders who bought near that level may sell into the rebound. Bitcoin trades far beyond US ETFs, so outflows are not proof of further downside, but a recovery that holds despite redemptions would be a stronger signal. Thanksgiving closes US markets, so the missing ETF data is not a sign of improved demand. Friday’s session will be more telling. The Bitcoin recovery above $60,000 is offering some relief after a brutal November sell-off, but the money flowing through US spot Bitcoin ETFs tells a less encouraging story. The funds recorded more than $2 billion in combined net outflows over four consecutive trading sessions ending November 24. Bitcoin’s return to the psychologically important price level follows a difficult week in which the cryptocurrency traded as low as approximately $55,300. The rebound is welcome. What is less clear is whether buyers have returned with enough capital to sustain it. Bitcoin ETFs Are Still Losing Money The scale of the recent withdrawals deserves more attention than the recovery itself. According to Farside Investors, US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $582.3 million on November 19, followed by another $669.2 million the next day. Withdrawals continued on Monday and Tuesday, bringing the combined total across those four trading sessions to approximately $2.05 billion. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for roughly $1.77 billion in net outflows during that period. Wednesday’s figures are still subject to final reporting confirmation, although available data points to further withdrawals. These numbers do not mean that every institutional investor is abandoning Bitcoin. ETF shareholders include different types of investors, from financial advisers and asset managers to individual traders. Some may be reducing risk, while others could be unwinding positions that were never intended as long-term investments. What the figures establish is that the ETF market has experienced persistent net redemptions, even after Bitcoin’s substantial decline. That is not the response bulls would ideally want to see from buyers following a major correction. Bitcoin’s Drop Below $60,000 Exposed a Deeper Problem Earlier this week, Bitcoin fell below $60,000 again after an initial recovery above $64,000 failed to hold. Glassnode’s November 24 report, titled The Canary in the Coal Mine, documented the severity of Bitcoin’s latest decline. The cryptocurrency reached approximately $55,300 on November 21, falling beneath the lows established during the summer. That matters because investors who bought during previous corrections may now be sitting on losses despite having entered the market at what appeared to be relatively attractive prices. Glassnode’s historical data reveals another uncomfortable detail. Long-term holders recently accounted for more than 75% of Bitcoin’s realized losses before their share fell back toward 50%. Similar periods of selling at a loss appeared during previous bear markets, although that alone does not establish that Bitcoin has reached a bottom. Their behavior becomes particularly important when Bitcoin starts recovering. Some holders may use a rebound to reduce their exposure or exit positions closer to their original purchase price. Others may be willing to hold through further volatility. Which group dominates will influence how much buying is required to sustain the next move higher. A price that previously attracted buyers can become an area of selling pressure when the market approaches it from below. This is one reason why reclaiming $60,000 should not automatically be interpreted as confirmation that the correction has ended. A Market Bottom Does Not Require Everyone to Turn Bullish There is a credible argument against interpreting persistent ETF outflows as evidence that Bitcoin must fall further. Markets can begin recovering before investor sentiment improves. In fact, waiting for every major indicator to turn positive can mean missing a substantial portion of a reversal. Glassnode’s latest research offers some historical perspective. Bitcoin’s realized losses relative to capital inflows over the preceding year have reached their highest intensity since the FTX collapse in 2022. Previous episodes of heavy losses have occurred near major market bottoms, but severe selling alone is not enough to confirm that a recovery is underway. Bitcoin also trades across a much broader market than US exchange-traded funds. Direct purchases, overseas exchanges and other investment vehicles can absorb selling even when American funds experience redemptions. The distinction is between evidence that a market can recover and evidence that it has already established a sustainable recovery. Bitcoin’s latest bounce demonstrates that buyers are willing to step in at lower prices. It does not yet establish whether those buyers can absorb additional selling at higher levels. If Bitcoin begins to hold its gains despite persistent ETF withdrawals, that would itself be an encouraging development. It would suggest that demand elsewhere in the market is capable of offsetting some of the pressure coming from the funds. For now, the price and ETF data leave that question open. Thanksgiving Could Make Bitcoin’s Next Move Harder to Read Thursday’s Thanksgiving holiday adds another complication to the recovery. US equity markets are closed, removing a regular trading session for American spot Bitcoin ETFs while cryptocurrency exchanges continue operating. The absence of new ETF flow figures during the holiday should not be confused with an improvement in institutional demand. With fewer traditional financial market participants active, Bitcoin’s immediate price movements may also provide an incomplete picture of how investors are responding to the recent sell-off. Friday’s shortened US trading session and the subsequent return to normal market hours will provide more useful evidence. For traders, the important signals are whether Bitcoin can retain its recent gains, whether ETF redemptions begin to ease and whether buying remains strong enough to absorb selling when normal market participation resumes. The $60,000 level may dominate the headlines, but the more convincing recovery will be the one that can survive without depending entirely on temporary relief from selling pressure.
content: Bitcoin has climbed back above $60,000 following a severe November sell-off that saw prices drop near $55,300.
